objectClass.notes: Static single-storey branded retail box on thaikit's shared 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 m module, exterior shell only. No interior geometry: glazing is a tinted mostly-opaque pane, not an opening. Nothing moves, so one root pivot and zero sockets is the correct contract. Distinguishing features on this plate: a hung brand fascia carrying a GREEN band over a white field over a BLUE trim, panelled at roughly 1 m centres; a mill-finish ALUMINIUM shopfront, not the near-black steel of the MK sibling; a BI-PARTING sliding entrance inside a BI-PARTING sliding entrance under a single transom that spans the four middle bays; a shopfront that TURNS THE CORNER onto the +X wall, with the fascia returning further still; a service door with a louvre at its foot and a small high window on that same wall; the green-and-blue vinyl decal band across every pane; and FOUR different rooftop units, not one repeated.

reasoning: Silhouette is a single rectangular prism -- low geometric complexity.
Richness is REPETITION and PANELLING, not intricate form. The instanced systems collapse the repeated parts into one InstancedMesh each.
Occlusion risk is real: the rear elevation is entirely unseen in the single plate.
Action readiness is minimal: static exterior shell, box collider, not breakable.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Repetition-dominated facade: without repetitionSystems the mullion and plant sets would each cost a draw call per part and blow maxDrawCalls=12.

The plate's glazing is TRANSPARENT and shows a full shop interior -- shelving, a chiller, a magazine rack, floor tiles. None of it is reproduced. It WAS, for one build: the plate's own shopfront rectified into the glazing plane and projected by world x/y, the same route the MK sibling uses. It was removed again on review. A baked interior is a flat picture on a flat pane -- it carries no parallax, so it slides against the framing as the camera orbits, and the mullions, rails and door stile printed into it argue with the ones this model builds as GEOMETRY at the same positions. The glazing ships as a tinted pane at #6F7371, which is also what the kit's exterior-shell rule asks for. The two homographies stay in the tree: they are what the shopfront was MEASURED from and remain the evidence for its layout. The decal band the image also carried is back as GEOMETRY, which is what it physically is -- vinyl applied to the outside of the glass -- so it has neither of the two faults that took the image off.

The shopfront is SEVEN verticals and ONE transom, and the count is what the last two builds got wrong. The first was a five-bay curtain wall -- an even grid, no entrance, no transom. The second invented a PROJECTING DOOR SURROUND standing 0.08 m proud between X -2.02 and +1.22, with 2.73 m jambs, its own head, a separate short transom mullion above that head, and a sidelight jamb: five parts describing a frame the plate does not have. The column scan settles it. -2.02 and +1.22 are ORDINARY full-height mullions of the same 0.065 m section as +2.41 and -0.83 -- four identical intermediates between two heavier corner posts, six verticals sill to head -- and the only vertical that stops short is the meeting stile at +0.255, which dies into the transom. The transom is a single 0.21 m rail from X -2.055 to +2.445, so the leftmost and rightmost bays are glazed full height and the four between them carry a light over the rail. A 0.48 m render pier closes the -X end.

The tall louvred rooftop unit stands about 0.25 m above the parapet in the plate. Here it tops out at 4.59, just under the parapet's 4.60, because 4.60 is the declared module ceiling and an overrun is a contract failure rather than a fidelity gain. The roofline is therefore unbroken; recorded as a deliberate departure.

The fascia panel joints and the render's rain streaking are carried as IMAGES, not geometry: the joints are drawn into the baked fascia (six seams at the x positions the rectified plate shows) and the streaking is a seamless 2.5 m tile on the wall material. Both are below the scale at which geometry would be worth a triangle at prop distance.

The wordmark is set in Liberation Sans Bold, a SUBSTITUTE for FamilyMart's own face, and the mark is drawn as two rounded bars, green over blue, from the plate. FamilyMart is a real trademark: the repo's MIT licence covers this asset's code, not the mark.

Zero coincident co-facing surface pairs (check-coplanar clean).
Exactly one root pivot and zero sockets; box collider; no destruction groups.
Every material declares textureless with named evidence.

silhouette.description: One rectangular prism with a parapet ring capping it at 4.60 all round. The silhouette events are the hung fascia standing 0.10 m proud of the parapet face and returning around the +X corner, the shopfront kerb, and the four rooftop units seen over the parapet.
silhouette.envelopeDerivation: x spans -4.00..+4.00 (parapet ring outer faces) = 8.00. y spans 0.00..4.60 = 4.60. z spans -3.50 (rear parapet) ..+3.50 = 7.00. The shell front face is set back to z=+2.50 so anything cantilevering off it lands ON the declared depth rather than overrunning it.
silhouette.meshyCrossCheck: Independent Meshy v7 reconstruction of the same plate is kept in scratch/ as evidence and was NOT used for the envelope: the declared 8.0 x 4.6 x 7.0 m is the kit's shared retail module across a dozen sibling props, a deliberate normalisation, and it is also what the rectification is anchored on. The measured build is 8.00 x 4.60 x 7.00 exactly.

viewEvidence.note: Rectified front. #E1E2E4 at standard deviation 1.8 over 9,660 px -- the cleanest crop on the prop.

Two homographies of the single plate, both written and documented in scratch/_retail/rect_fm.py: the FRONT elevation rectified over X -4.00..+4.00 by Y 0..4.395 at 200 px/m, and the +X SIDE over Z +3.50..-3.50 by Y 0..4.60. Each is bounded by lines fitted from pixel scans -- the fascia green band top (y = 308 + 0.107(x-90)), the building base (y = 598.5 + 0.2833x, taken from the four columns where the white kerb separates from the contact SHADOW), and the near corner at x=663 found as the slope break in the green line. componentTree.name: Building shell
componentTree.topologyRationale: One continuous render skin over four walls. Splitting it per elevation would cost a draw call per wall for the life of the prop to express one material.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Solid box, x -3.94..+3.94, y 0..3.55, z -3.44..+2.50. SOLID, not a ring: the prop is an exterior shell only ever seen from outside, so an interior would cost draw calls, geometries and VRAM for something nobody sees. Solid also means the shopfront needs no opening cut in it, which removes all four reveal faces and the z-fighting they cause.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Set 0.06 m INSIDE the parapet ring on every elevation (walls at +-3.94 and -3.44; parapet at +-4.00 and -3.50). That difference is a coping drip edge, and it is what stops a wall face and a parapet face being coplanar and co-facing.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Flat painted cement render, roughness 0.94, metalness 0.0, no procedural texture set. The rain streaking is a seamless 2.5 m post-construction tile in multiplier space, world-planar by face normal so a 7 m wall and a 0.24 m coping carry the same physical tile size.

pivot.name: root
pivot.notes: base-center, as the asset declares. A STATIC exterior shell: nothing opens, turns or swings, so one root pivot is the whole mechanism inventory and that is the correct answer, not a gap.

collider.notes: Declared on the asset as box. One convex proxy over the whole envelope; a level builder collides with the building, not with its canopy plates.

componentTree.name: Roof deck
componentTree.topologyRationale: A flat deck plane. Its own component only because the membrane is a visibly different value from the wall render, and this prop is seen from above in every hero shot.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Thin slab spanning y 3.50..3.62, overlapping UNDER the parapet ring.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Spans y 3.50..3.62 so its underside is sunk INTO the shell rather than resting on it. Authored flush, the deck bottom face and the parapet ring bottom face would both sit at y=3.550 facing down -- tens of square metres of coplanar co-facing surface, and exactly the pair check-coplanar catches.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: Membrane slab spanning y 3.50..3.62, a value below the walls so it reads as a different surface from above.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Parapet ring and fascia wall
componentTree.topologyRationale: A continuous upstand ring in one material, with the front simply taller -- which a plan extrusion cannot express, since an extrude carries one height. Merged boxes are the right primitive, and anything else in the same material folds in here rather than costing its own submission.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Front fascia wall plus left, right and rear upstands, merged into ONE component and ONE draw call, with same-material cladding folded in.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: The ring is pulled in to x +-3.975, not the template's +-4.00: on the +X elevation the FASCIA turns the corner and is the outermost thing there. At +-4.00 the upstand stood 0.01 m proud of the return board and hid it outright -- the azimuth-90 frame showed a bare wall with the blue trim peeking out below the parapet's foot. The outward stack on that elevation is wall 3.94 < parapet 3.975 < frame 3.985 < door fittings 3.995 < fascia 4.000.
geometryDescriptor.mergeNote: Primitive is "box" because the schema enumerates primitives, but this is a MERGED cluster built into one BufferGeometry and submitted as ONE draw call.

colorMaterialRecipe.recipe: The SAME render as the shell -- one material, not two. Front band y 3.55..4.60 plus FULL-HEIGHT side and rear upstands to 4.60 (the siblings' 0.40 m kerb would have left the plate's parapet a third of its height), the shopfront's -X render pier, and the plinth under the whole building, all folded in at one draw call.

actionProfile.notes: Rigidly parented to the root. NO pivot and NO socket, deliberately: this part does not move and nothing attaches to it.

componentTree.name: Brand fascia panel
componentTree.topologyRationale: One panel carrying the brand band on two elevations. Authored UVs are what keep it at one material and one draw call: each board names the face that samples the canvas band and every other face samples the plain white field in the bottom 12.5%.

geometryDescriptor.topologyIntent: Hung brand fascia across the front and returning 2.55 m onto the +X wall.
geometryDescriptor.zFightingNote: Panel width 7.98, not 8.00: at 8.00 its own +-X faces would be coplanar and co-facing with the parapet upstands and overlapping them in y. Its body 3.38..3.50 is sunk into the parapet front face at 3.40 and stands proud to the envelope edge.

The roofline is unbroken -- the plate's tall louvred unit stands above its parapet and here tops out at 4.59 under the declared ceiling, recorded as a deliberate departure.

featureReviews.evidence: SEVEN verticals and ONE transom, counted by column scan of the rectified front in three separate height bands (Y 1.55..1.85, 2.30..2.50, 2.95..3.15 at threshold luma 130) that agree to within 0.03 m: -3.37 w0.15, -2.02 w0.065, -0.83 w0.065, +0.255 w0.125, +1.21 w0.065, +2.41 w0.070, +3.72 w0.19. SIX run sill 0.05 to head 3.36. The seventh, +0.255, is present in the 1.55 and 2.30 bands and ABSENT from the 2.95 one -- it is the sliding pair's meeting stile and it stops at the transom, which is how it is built (Y 0.10..2.60). The transom is a single 0.21 m rail at Y 2.56..2.77; a row scan of that band puts its ends at X -2.05 and +2.44, so it spans the four middle bays and dies into the mullions, leaving the left and right bays glazed full height. The sensor plate sits on it at X -0.02..+0.34, also scanned.
featureReviews.notes: Two builds got the count wrong and this is the correction. The first had no entrance at all -- five identical glazed bays and a flat pane where the door is. The second invented a PROJECTING DOOR SURROUND between X -2.02 and +1.22: 2.73 m jambs standing 0.08 m proud, its own head, a short transom mullion above that head, and a sidelight jamb -- five parts describing a frame the plate does not have, and the reason the shopfront read as a box hung on the glass. -2.02 and +1.21 are ordinary full-height mullions of the same 0.065 m section as -0.83 and +2.41. Removing the surround took a draw call and a geometry off the prop as well.

featureReviews.evidence: Mill-finish aluminium #D4D6D5 (standard deviation 11.2 on the rectified kick rail), not the MK sibling's near-black steel. Verticals at the SCANNED X -3.34, -2.02, -0.83, +0.255, +1.21, +2.41 and +3.80 -- an uneven rhythm of 1.32, 1.19, 1.09, 0.96, 1.20 and 1.39 m, not a grid -- and four of the seven share one 0.065 m section and are therefore one InstancedMesh of four rather than four boxes in the merge. The shopfront TURNS THE CORNER: glazing 0.95 m and framing onto the +X wall, with the fascia returning 2.55 m. The FamilyMart green-over-blue decal band runs at Y 1.15..1.27 across the panes, both sliding leaves and the return -- eight merged boxes on ONE white material carrying per-box vertex colours, because a material per colour would have put the prop over its ceiling of 8.
featureReviews.notes: Scored below the other criticals for one reason. The plate's glazing is transparent and shows a full shop interior -- shelving, a chiller, a magazine rack, the FamilyMart decal stripe -- and none of it ships. It DID, for one build, as the plate's own shopfront rectified into the glazing plane and projected by world x/y, the same route MK uses; it was removed on review because a baked interior is a flat picture on a flat pane. It carries no parallax, so it slides against the framing as the camera orbits, and the mullions and rails printed into it argue with the ones this model builds as geometry at the same positions. The pane ships tinted at #6F7371, the darkest tone that clears the turntable gate at all four azimuths, which is also what the kit's exterior-shell rule asks for. The two homographies stay in the tree: they are what the layout above was measured from. The decal stripe went with the image and is the one identity feature this prop no longer carries.

featureReviews.evidence: Service door leaf at Z +0.78..-0.28 by Y 0..2.40 with a louvre at its foot and a lever at 1.15, and a 0.85 x 0.66 m window at Z -2.93..-2.08 -- all read off the +X rectification, all in ONE painted-steel component because the plate measures the door leaf (#3E4346) and the window glass (#3D3F3E) at the same value.
featureReviews.notes: Two corrections. The steel was first lifted 1.43x for the hole gate and at luma 146 the door rendered at 118 against a 129 wall and stopped reading as a door, where the plate has it at 0.59 of its wall; it ships at 116. And the window pane, set back 3 cm in a reveal, rendered at luma 69 at azimuth 90 -- 0.63 of its albedo where the wall beside it manages 0.88 -- and the turntable gate read the 103 x 68 px opening as background punched through the wall. Flush with its surround it clears. Deliberately NOT mirrored onto the -X wall, which the plate never shows.

featureReviews.evidence: FOUR different units in one merged galvanised component: a hooded duct run with two brackets, a wall-type condenser behind a square fan guard with a cylinder cowl, a riser box with a conduit drop, and a tall louvred tower with a louvre face and a cap.
featureReviews.notes: The first build carried ONE bank. The template's instanced condenser system is left EMPTY here, which is a legitimate answer rather than a missing config: instancing one casing three times is one draw call and so is merging four different ones, so the repetition would have cost fidelity to save nothing. Plan positions are read through a Y=4.60 homography of the roof and are the softest numbers on the prop -- the plant sits a metre below that plane -- so they are reported at 0.74 confidence.

reviewHistory.summary: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.93 -- not a pass self-score. 780/16000 triangles, 10/12 draw calls, 8/8 materials, 10/16 unique geometries, 2 textures. The shopfront correction made the prop CHEAPER: deleting the invented door surround took its InstancedMesh with it, and folding the four intermediate mullions into the one system that remained left ten draw calls and ten geometries against eleven of each. Materials stay at the ceiling of 8, and the decal band is what put them there -- one white material carrying two brand colours as per-box vertex colours instead of two materials.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Real-time browser FPS prop on low-end integrated GPUs; a level builder places hundreds at once. All four ceilings come from thaikit resolveBudget() for the hero2x class and none was invented. The component split was costed against the DRAW-CALL ceiling in the blockout, before any geometry existed: parts that share a material are merged into one component rather than left to be merged later, because a pivot hung off a part cannot be merged afterwards.

drawCalls.note: Ten draw calls of twelve. Nine merged components and ONE InstancedMesh system: the aluminium shopfront is 21 boxes in one submission, the rooftop plant 12 primitives in another, and the parapet carries the front band, three upstands, the render pier and the plinth.

materials.note: wall is shared by the shell AND the parapet -- one render skin, one shader. steel is shared by the service door, its louvre, its lever and the side window's pane, which the plate measures at the same value. alu is shared by the merged frame and the four instanced mullions. Eight materials of eight -- at the ceiling, and the decal band is what put it there rather than the two materials a green and a blue would otherwise have cost.

uniqueGeometries.note: One per component plus one per repetition system. A scaled box is NOT a shared geometry -- the generator bakes real dimensions in via geometry.scale(), so every differently-sized box is genuinely distinct. Each InstancedMesh reuses a single geometry across all its instances, which is the whole point.

triangles.note: Triangles are NOT the binding constraint on this prop -- draw calls are. The headroom is deliberately spent on silhouette quality (chamfers, cowl segments, shutter ribs) and must not be read as room to split components, which would spend the axis that is actually scarce.

lightingFromPhoto.notes: The plate is a flat studio lightbox: surfaces at 90 degrees to each other measure within a few levels, which is only possible under near-shadowless illumination. That is WHY the measured crop means are usable as albedo with little correction.
High fill ratio inferred from the shadow-side wall retaining full value.

The seamless backdrop acts as a large uniform environment. The thaikit harness supplies NO environment map, which is why every metal on this prop carries a metalness well below its physical value -- a metal with nothing to reflect renders black.
NO rim light in the plate. Recorded so a missing rim in the render is not read as a defect.
Exposure 1.0 with ACES filmic tone mapping; no exposure compensation is applied to the measured albedos and none is warranted.

NO contact or ground shadow in the plate -- it is a cut-out against a seamless backdrop. Recorded so the absence is not read as a missing feature. IN USE this is a floor-placed building and the HOST scene owns its contact shadow: castShadow ships enabled on every mesh and the factory defines no ground plane of its own.

proceduralStrategy.strategy: box, cylinder and merged-box clusters only. No organic surfaces exist on this subject.

ONE InstancedMesh system carrying four parts: the shopfront's four intermediate mullions, one 0.065 x 3.07 x 0.08 m section at the four scanned x. The previous build had two systems, and the second -- an 'entrance surround' of two 2.73 m jambs -- described a frame the plate does not have and is gone. The condenser system is deliberately EMPTY -- the plate shows four genuinely different rooftop units, so they are merged geometry instead, which is also one draw call and costs nothing in fidelity.
All procedural variation is assigned by instance INDEX, never from a random source, so the model is byte-identical on every build.

Every material is declared textureless. The brand fascia receives its wordmark as a generated canvas assigned AFTER material construction -- the documented route for a printed brand fascia, unaffected by the declaration.

risks.description: Rear and left elevations are not in the single plate; authored plain.

The plate shows a full shop interior and the decal stripe through the glazing; the shipped pane is flat tinted glass, so both are absent. A baked interior was built and removed: it has no parallax and its printed framing fights the geometry.
risks.mitigation: Recorded in assumptions with the reason. The upgrade path, if it is wanted, is geometry behind the glass or a parallax-mapped shader, not a flat photograph.
